comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
A concrete use case landed for this, which is why it moves up: an agent
in a pane acting as integrator for a parallel workflow - splitting panes
below itself, starting an agent in each, and briefing them. See the card
that records it.

Verified today that the *backend* half of that needs nothing from us:
`$HERDR_PANE_ID` tells a pane where it is, and `herdr pane split`,
`pane rename` and `pane run` do the rest, from inside the pane. So this
card is precisely the remainder - focus, zoom, which tab a region shows,
the sidebar - and the remainder is exactly the part herdr cannot reach,
because Muster's keyboard cursor is view-local by design.

One addition to the description: **an agent has no eyes.** A person can
see which panes are on screen and where focus is; an agent must ask. The
read side ("what is this window showing") is at least as important as the
write side, and a CLI that only writes leaves an agent arranging a window
it cannot look at.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**This is the agent surface, and herdr's CLI explicitly is not** - worth
recording as a decision rather than leaving to be re-litigated whenever
somebody notices that shelling out to `herdr` from a pane already works.

It does already work, which is the temptation. But it cannot express a
window that spans two daemons - `herdr` in a pane reaches that pane's
daemon and no other, so nothing can put a pane on the devenv or ask what
the window is showing. It silently truncates anything with a view
consequence, because a split made behind Muster's back appears but
focuses nothing. And a documented herdr-shaped agent surface would *be*
the contract regardless of what the seam says, which is the one thing
"we never let one own our contract" rules out. Nothing depends on it yet;
that is what makes this cheap to settle now.

**Ergonomics is the point, not coverage.** Not one verb per herdr verb -
a vocabulary shaped to what Muster means to support, where one intent is
one call. The sharpest evidence: driving this by hand needs a `sleep`
between creating a pane and typing into it, because a pane's program is
spawned with the pane and text sent before its shell draws a prompt races
the first output. The suite already carries a comment about that hazard,
having been caught by it. Every agent scripting this by hand would
rediscover that wait and get it wrong under load. "Make a pane below me,
in this directory, running this" as a single call moves the race into one
place that gets it right, and that is the kind of thing this CLI is for.

**Reads are half the job.** An agent has no eyes: it cannot see which
panes are on screen or where focus is, so it must be able to ask. A CLI
that only writes leaves an agent arranging a window it cannot look at.

**Addressing needs designing with this, not after.** The CLI has to reach
a running GUI process, and something has to say which window. A `MUSTER_*`
variable carried into panes answers that and announces the surface at the
same time, so `muster` needs no `--window` flag from inside a pane.

creator: Alexander Terp
description: Desideratum 9. Backend ops already have herdr's CLI; this covers view ops - focus, arrange, window management - so agents can drive muster the way they drive herdr.
title: muster CLI: drive the view layer from scripts and agents
